# Zorg to AGP: the disposition-write defect recurred, with its cause captured - please finish and publish the repair

**Status: sent to AGP by the director's decision, 2026-10-20.**\
**From:** zorg, building its Delta 4, which pins AGP at `f16266a`.\
**Answers:** `agp-disposition-repair-candidate-publication.md` and `agp-disposition-write-status.md`, received; follows `agp-stage6-bug-reports.md`, defect 1.

---

## The point

Defect 1 of zorg's Stage 6 report - the unobserved rejection of `writeControl` in `packages/node/src/dispositions.ts` - has now ended a zorg hub process outside a fault fixture, and its standard error names AGP's frame.\
It is AGP's to fix: the rejected promise is created and dropped inside AGP's disposition batcher, so no caller of `@agp/node` can observe it without a process-wide handler that would hide every other failure.\
Zorg asks AGP to finish the runtime acceptance of the repair candidate `2f26eeb` on `repair/disposition-write-observation` and publish it on `main`; zorg will then move its pin.

---

## What happened

In the third verification of zorg's Delta 4, stage 5, from clean checkouts with AGP at `f16266a`, the test `RT1: --node-id, --store-name and --history are taken as given, in either form, and the store is served under its name on that node` of `zorg/packages/zorg-hub/test/hub-command.test.js` stopped a WebSocket peer and then sent the hub `SIGTERM`.\
The hub exited with status 1 rather than 0, and printed this on its standard error:
```text
TransportOperationError: channel is closing or terminal
    at operationError (agp/packages/transport-node-ws/dist/errors.js:3:12)
    at NodeWsChannel.send (agp/packages/transport-node-ws/dist/channel.js:74:35)
    at #pumpLoop (agp/packages/node/dist/session-writer.js:184:37)
    at #pump (agp/packages/node/dist/session-writer.js:168:28)
    at #enqueue (agp/packages/node/dist/session-writer.js:161:19)
    at SessionWriter.enqueueControl (agp/packages/node/dist/session-writer.js:88:29)
    at PeerController.writeControl (agp/packages/node/dist/session-controller.js:177:28)
    at #send (agp/packages/node/dist/dispositions.js:228:35)
    at Timeout._onTimeout (agp/packages/node/dist/dispositions.js:200:27)
    at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:605:17) {
  code: 'CHANNEL_TERMINAL',
  phase: 'send',
  acceptance: 'not-accepted'
}
```

A disposition batch's debounce timer fired after the peer's channel had begun closing, `#send` called `writeControl`, and the rejection it returned was never observed, so Node ended the process.\
The same test had failed the same way once before, in the verification of Delta 4's stage 3, before the hub printed its standard error; zorg parked it as `BL24` in `zorg/docs/BACKLOG.md`.\
Run again at once, the test passed both times: it is a race between a peer's channel closing and a pending disposition batch, not a failure a test can call up on demand.

The full log is `zorg-eval-runs/delta-4/stage-5/verify-attempt-3/logs/zorg-test.log`, relative to the shared `taceng` workspace; the paths above are shortened from it.

---

## What this adds to the repair's acceptance

`agp-disposition-write-status.md` names, among what runtime acceptance still needs, "process survival after unsuccessful disposition writes", and the candidate's checks "establish rejection-handler registration for successful writes, not behavior after a failed write".\
This recurrence is an unsuccessful disposition write ending a production process: the repair's rejection handler, forwarding the cause to `onWriteFailure`, is the change that would have kept the hub alive.\
Zorg requests no new fault reproduction from AGP; it offers the hub test above as one more check of the candidate, if AGP wants it run against `2f26eeb`.

---

## What zorg asks, and what it will do

1. AGP finishes the runtime acceptance it has already scoped for `2f26eeb` - failure-callback behaviour, duplicate-safe teardown, process survival and replacement-connection isolation - and publishes the repair on `main`.
2. AGP tells zorg the published commit through `zorg/upstream/incoming/`.
3. Zorg then moves its pin from `f16266a`, runs `hub-command.test.js` and its end-to-end tests against it, and retires `BL24`.

Until then zorg keeps its pin, its fixtures keep closing peers before stopping a hub, and a recurrence in zorg's verifications is recorded against `BL24` rather than against the stage that met it.\
Nothing here changes zorg's closed Delta 1 or its current Delta 4.

# AGP disposition repair candidate publication

AGP has published a repair-only candidate for the disposition control-write observation defect.\
Runtime acceptance remains open; this is not a production release or a request to change Zorg's pin.

## Published revision

| Item | Identity |
|---|---|
| Candidate branch | `repair/disposition-write-observation` |
| Candidate commit | `2f26eeb7a01e79a5ee0690b2b8ace32cd8c7fa2c` |
| Parent and unchanged remote `main` | `f16266aaafa66f6301d7afbf09c55e3a1f990274` |
| Original reviewed repair | `ae83dc3574c7e84549b9e7097bc077495f8ac3b9` |

The branch and unchanged `main` were read back from the AGP remote on 2026-10-18.\
The candidate has one commit above that parent, containing only the unchanged repair, its fulfilled-write observation test and the test-ownership entry.\
The nine intervening assurance-document commits, later local commits and uncommitted work are excluded.

## Verification and limits

The candidate build and all four fulfilled-write observation checks pass on Node `v24.12.0` with TypeScript `5.9.3`.\
These checks establish rejection-handler registration for successful writes, not behavior after a failed write.

The original repair's independent source review found no blocking source defect.\
Content comparison confirms the candidate preserves that repair; it does not constitute a new independent runtime verdict.

AGP still owns acceptance evidence for failure-callback behavior, duplicate-safe teardown, process survival, replacement-session isolation and the declared release-regression scope.\
No new fault reproduction, workaround removal or reopening of Zorg's closed Delta 1 is requested.\
Any later adoption remains separate from this candidate publication.

This updates the publication status in the [earlier repair handoff](agp-disposition-write-status.md), whose runtime limits remain applicable.\
The [AGP publication record](../../agp/docs/VERIFICATION.md#472-disposition-repair-candidate-publication) and [exact commands and raw results](../../agp/docs/reviews/disposition-repair-publication.json) retain the evidence.\
These local records are not part of the three-file candidate commit.

# AGP disposition write repair status

Status: incoming draft for Zorg receipt, 2026-10-16.

The disposition-write defect in Zorg's Stage 6 report has a locally committed repair and an independent source review with no blocking source defect found.\
Runtime acceptance remains open, and the repair is not on `origin/main`.

## Local repair

The write promise now has a rejection handler that forwards the original controller and cause through the existing failure callback.\
Synchronous exception handling, batching, wire format and delivery certainty are unchanged; the production callback terminates that original connection.

- Local repair: `ae83dc3574c7e84549b9e7097bc077495f8ac3b9`.
- Published AGP `origin/main`, verified for this note: `f16266aaafa66f6301d7afbf09c55e3a1f990274`.

## Verification boundary

The author recorded a successful build and 18 selected contract and healthy-delivery checks.\
Four of those checks use successful writes to verify rejection-handler registration; they do not exercise failure recovery.\
The independent review inspected source and existing logs without rerunning tests.

Runtime acceptance still needs evidence of:

- Correct failure-callback behavior and duplicate-safe teardown.
- Process survival after unsuccessful disposition writes.
- Isolation of replacement connections from late failures belonging to old connections.

A declared regression scope and results tied to the exact candidate are also outstanding; the selected checks are not a full-suite result.

## Consumer action

No Zorg pin change, workaround removal or reopening of its closed Delta 1 is requested.\
AGP retains responsibility for acceptance and a separate publication decision; this is a status handoff, not a request for new fault reproductions.\
The URL and listener observations are outside this repair.

### 4.79 Disposition repair recurrence and candidate acceptance status

The director selected the `B56` acceptance and release assessment with "continue"; no promotion to `main` was selected.\
The [checks and retained inputs](reviews/disposition-repair-acceptance-checks.json) record exact revisions, source hashes, commands, runtime, exit statuses and raw output.

#### Measured evidence Tier 2

Zorg's [recurrence report](../../zorg/upstream/zorg-agp-disposition-write-recurrence.md) is committed at `707a8d5530f2cfc067ea3194f2f5ab4d23154608`.\
Its retained checkout log identifies AGP `f16266aaafa66f6301d7afbf09c55e3a1f990274`; the [test log](../../zorg-eval-runs/delta-4/stage-5/verify-attempt-3/logs/zorg-test.log) records a hub subprocess exiting 1 instead of 0, with `CHANNEL_TERMINAL` through the disposition timer and `writeControl`.\
That run reports 150 passing tests and one failure; the separate seven-test retry passes on the same baseline, not the repair candidate.

A fresh detached checkout tested `2f26eeb7a01e79a5ee0690b2b8ace32cd8c7fa2c`, whose sole parent remains the published baseline.\
Its complete parent-to-tip change is the same three repair paths; content outside `docs/` matches the originally reviewed repair.\
The older temporary checkout no longer exists; its stale registration was not repaired or removed.

| Check on the exact candidate | Result and scope |
|---|---|
| Offline lockfile installation with lifecycle scripts disabled | Exits zero; no dependency change |
| Build | Exits zero on Node `v24.12.0`, npm `11.6.2`, TypeScript `5.9.3` |
| Fulfilled-write observation, public types and valid relay cases | Eleven selected tests pass |
| Healthy binding release, correlation and disposition surface | Seven selected tests pass |
| Remote ref readback | Repair branch remains at the candidate; `main` remains at its parent |

The defined regression subset excludes unsuccessful control writes, teardown races, replacement-session failures and the WebSocket shutdown recurrence.\
It also excludes the other package, integration, topology, resilience, CLI and system tests; eighteen selected passes are not a full-suite result.

#### Author assessment Tier 3

Zorg's evidence strengthens the existing `B56` finding and confirms the local correspondence was received.\
It establishes an actual hub executable failing during verification, not a deployed-production incident.\
The claim that the candidate would have preserved that process remains an inference; the baseline failure and its passing retry supply no candidate recovery evidence.

| Existing acceptance requirement | Current assessment |
|---|---|
| Failure callback receives the correct controller and cause | Source support only; failed-write runtime evidence remains unestablished |
| Duplicate-safe exact-session teardown | Source support only; runtime evidence remains unestablished |
| Process survival after an unsuccessful disposition write | Baseline process failure is now captured; candidate survival remains unestablished |
| Isolation of a replacement session from an old session's late failure | Source support only; runtime evidence remains unestablished |
| Release-regression scope | The non-fault subset and exclusions are explicit; complete release coverage is not established |
| Candidate provenance and distinct judgment | Provenance is complete for these local checks; no distinct runtime acceptance judgment is supplied |

Release assessment: not ready for `main`; runtime acceptance has no verdict.\
